relations.subject: role:eventing-full-admin
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - extraction-layer predicate already minted by the Capella twin, not yet promoted
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server version 7.0.0 or earlier, Eventing always ran with `Full Admin` privileges. This prevented broader adoption as the role allowed creating new users and escalating privileges. The new `Eventing Full Admin` role removes the ability to create users or modify credentials, improving security while still supporting the required Eventing operations.

relations.subject: eventing:bucket-alias-binding
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: A highly useful special case allows an Eventing Function to perform direct self-recursion by creating a Read-Write binding to its own source collection for document enrichment operations. In this case, the Eventing framework detects and suppresses the direct self-recursive mutations. This capability applies only to the aliased JavaScript map and is not supported for mutations generated through SQL++.

notable_absence.finding: As on the Capella twin, zero mentions of any Capella management-plane role or Advanced-credential privilege anywhere on this page - every access-control reference is to the classic Server RBAC axis (Full Admin/Eventing Full Admin/generic 'admin privileges'), confirming the two systems run side by side rather than merging.

cross_component_finding: This Server page is measurably richer than the Capella twin on shared sections: the worker-sizing guidance here includes the exact dynamically-generated warning message text ('There are 104 eventing workers configured to run on 24 cores...'), a concrete concurrency formula (4x cores / 2x vCPUs), full LCB_ETMPFAIL troubleshooting with retry counts, residency-ratio guidance with a concrete example (12K mutations/sec, 18% threshold), and a regex-escaping gotcha - none of which appear in the twin's concepts/relations despite the shared heading list. This is the same completeness-gap pattern already documented for eventing-lifecycle.json, eventing-timers.json and eventing-Terminologies.json in this batch, now recurring a fourth time.
cross_product_finding: This page has a dedicated opening section, 'What Are the Recommendations Before Starting an Upgrade?', instructing the reader to pause all Eventing Functions before starting a Couchbase Server upgrade to reduce rebalance duration. The Capella twin's heading list (grepped directly) has no equivalent section at all - its only upgrade-related sentence is a passing reassurance that 'all upgrades will carry forward the configured number of workers... so you don't have to worry about a production system slowing down during an upgrade.' This is a clean, structural difference rather than a documentation gap: on Server, the customer initiates and controls the upgrade and therefore needs pre-upgrade guidance; on Capella, Couchbase performs the upgrade, so there is no 'before you start an upgrade' customer action to document - Capella's docs only need to reassure the user that an upgrade they do not control will not disrupt their Function's worker configuration.
